problem_text:
A manufacturing consortium is tasked with devising a strategy to curtail cumulative defect generation across a network of eight production lines. At present, no corrective interventions are in place.

The baseline characteristics for each assembly line are detailed as follows:
* For Line A, the defect rate per unit is 2.914, with an output volume of 161.445.
* For Line B, the defect rate per unit is 1.576, with an output volume of 147.784.
* For Line C, the defect rate per unit is 0.526, with an output volume of 243.086.
* For Line D, the defect rate per unit is 1.147, with an output volume of 197.147.
* For Line E, the defect rate per unit is 1.777, with an output volume of 175.116.
* For Line F, the defect rate per unit is 1.797, with an output volume of 136.242.
* For Line G, the defect rate per unit is 1.951, with an output volume of 56.141.
* For Line H, the defect rate per unit is 1.938, with an output volume of 76.137.

To address the defect issue, eight distinct quality enhancement protocols can be implemented, each offering a specific percentage reduction in the defect rate:
* Protocol Alpha reduces defects by 57%.
* Protocol Beta reduces defects by 13%.
* Protocol Gamma reduces defects by 81%.
* Protocol Delta reduces defects by 15%.
* Protocol Epsilon reduces defects by 79%.
* Protocol Zeta reduces defects by 65%.
* Protocol Eta reduces defects by 54%.
* Protocol Theta reduces defects by 74%.

Deploying a protocol on a given line incurs a supplementary cost per unit of output. The comprehensive matrix of costs for every line-protocol pairing is provided:

| Line \ Protocol | Alpha | Beta | Gamma | Delta | Epsilon | Zeta | Eta | Theta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line A | 101.756 | 100.471 | 93.252 | 142.385 | 70.593 | 67.05 | 163.935 | 31.866 |
| Line B | 171.344 | 133.114 | 138.656 | 41.227 | 196.941 | 56.343 | 43.146 | 40.426 |
| Line C | 116.371 | 192.108 | 54.053 | 86.959 | 45.046 | 131.691 | 92.106 | 15.547 |
| Line D | 126.68 | 47.492 | 122.519 | 83.879 | 143.9 | 49.099 | 152.942 | 163.659 |
| Line E | 21.887 | 29.333 | 175.676 | 45.522 | 71.937 | 96.935 | 59.847 | 173.901 |
| Line F | 110.266 | 131.431 | 123.424 | 126.149 | 121.531 | 76.106 | 170.648 | 127.299 |
| Line G | 164.61 | 144.138 | 66.515 | 126.752 | 26.103 | 35.45 | 32.394 | 68.022 |
| Line H | 44.778 | 141.753 | 107.057 | 89.465 | 36.195 | 82.905 | 45.293 | 130.745 |

The consortium must determine which protocols to apply to each line; a single line may employ multiple protocols concurrently, and it is permissible for a line to remain partially untreated. The primary objective is to guarantee that the aggregate defect count is diminished by a minimum proportion of R = 0.547 relative to the initial baseline, all while minimizing the total implementation expenditure.
